chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them) said:

A Bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who was called Qulayb, and he said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, I prepared for Hajj so many times, but it was not decreed for me.' So he said to him: 'O Qulayb, upon you is Friday, for it is the Hajj of the poor.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Friday prayer as the 'Hajj of the poor' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) advises the Bedouin Qulayb, who was unable to perform Hajj due to repeated impediments, to prioritize Friday prayer, declaring it the 'Hajj of the poor.' This narration underscores the spiritual equivalence of the weekly congregational prayer to the annual pilgrimage for those lacking the means or opportunity, a concept deeply valued in Shia jurisprudence for maintaining ritual continuity. The emphasis on Friday as a substitute highlights the communal and devotional aspects of worship that transcend physical travel.
